newsitem.title: USA: EchoStar files suit against News Corp..
newsitem.headline: EchoStar files suit against News Corp..

text.p: Satellite TV firm EchoStar Communications Corp. said Monday it amended a breach-of-contract suit against media giant News Corp., further unravelling a $1 billion deal the companies signed in February.
EchoStar said it seeks damages resulting from News Corp.'s "many uncured material breaches" of the agreement, including "lost profits" it said could exceed $5 billion.

EchoStar said because of News Corp.'s alleged failure to meet its obligations, which include a $200 million loan, it cannot fulfil its business plan. EchoStar said it has consulted investment banking firms regarding methods of meeting its capital needs.
EchoStar also said it intends to speak with major vendors and other potential strategic partners. It said it believes it can arrange transactions to meet short- and medium-term obligations.
News Corp. declined comment. "We have no comment other than to say we will contest the matter in court," a spokesman said.
Asked whether there was any chance the agreement could be kept alive, a spokesman said it was "very unlikely."
Asked whether News Corp. was considering an alliance with EchoStar competitor PrimeStar, the spokesman declined to coment, except to say, "There are a lot of options we're looking."
PrimeStar is a satellite-TV company controlled by Tele-Communications Inc., Time Warner Inc., Comcast Corp. and Cox Communications Inc.

The admendment to the breach-of-contract suit expands a May 8 suit filed by EchoStar in the U.S. District Court for the District of Colorado. In that suit, it sought a declaratory judgment confirming the obligations of News Corp. to make the $200 million loan.
In February, News Corp. agreed to pay $1 billion in cash and assets for a 50 percent stake in EchoStar.

The venture, which was to offer up to 500 channels of digital TV, Internet services and local broadcast TV signals to U.S. markets, began to crumble not long after it was signed. EchoStar stock was off 62.5 cents at $13 on the Nasdaq in early afternoon trading.
